fomc-2026-09.standing: The rate-setting committee of the US central bank, which meets eight times a year to set the overnight federal funds rate. It anchors the dollar's price and short-term borrowing costs worldwide, so its decisions carry far beyond American borders.
fomc-2026-09.recent: The committee meets after a war-driven supply shock turned the argument upside down: Houthis captured Yemen's port of Mocha, oil jumped to $105, and August consumer prices rose 0.4%. Goldman Sachs abandoned its no-hike call, and an August payroll surge pushed hike odds to two-in-three. At issue is whether a conflict the Fed cannot reach belongs in the policy rate.

boe-2026-09.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, which meets eight times a year to set Bank Rate and votes member by member, with the split published alongside the decision. Bank Rate feeds through to UK mortgages, business lending and the pound.
boe-2026-09.recent: The committee meets with oil near $110 a barrel and long-dated government bond yields at multi-decade highs worldwide — a combination that pushes on imported inflation and on the cost of financing the UK's own borrowing at the same time. The decision settles what British borrowers pay while that pressure builds from outside.

boj-2026-09.standing: Japan's central bank, whose policy board meets eight times a year to set the short-term policy rate and steer government bond yields. It anchors borrowing costs in the world's largest creditor nation, and the yen moves with it.
boj-2026-09.recent: Tokyo has been weighing whether to steer the currency through pension money — a yen defence run outside the central bank entirely — and the yen has since surged as the dollar slid to its weakest since May. That leaves the board's own instrument, the policy rate, as what this meeting settles.

uk-cpi-2026-10.standing: The Office for National Statistics' monthly measure of UK consumer prices, published mid-month for the month before. It is the number the Bank of England's inflation target is written against, and it sets the uprating of pensions, benefits and index-linked gilts.
uk-cpi-2026-10.recent: The release lands into a global repricing rather than a domestic one: the 10-year Treasury yield has reached 5%, oil has extended gains on Mideast supply fears, and petrol costs drove a sharp inflation increase in the US in August. September is the month whose figure conventionally anchors the following year's benefit uprating, so this print settles more than the rate path.

fomc-2026-10.standing: The rate-setting meeting of the US central bank's Federal Open Market Committee, held eight times a year to set the federal funds target. It is the reference price for dollar credit worldwide, and borrowing costs from mortgages to emerging-market debt move off it.
fomc-2026-10.recent: The committee arrives at this meeting arguing over a supply shock rather than a slowdown: oil near $105 a barrel pushed August consumer prices up 0.4%, while a payroll surge removed the labour-market cover for standing still. Goldman Sachs abandoned its no-hike call, and the question is whether an oil-driven price rise warrants a response at all.

ecb-2026-10.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council, which sets the single policy rate for the twenty countries sharing the euro. It meets roughly every six weeks, and its decisions set borrowing costs for some 350 million people across economies with very different exposures.
ecb-2026-10.recent: The council's argument is whether an energy shock reaches wages and prices a second time, or passes through once and fades — Deutsche Bank has already raised its expected ECB peak to 2.75% on that risk. With Brent near $110 a barrel, this meeting settles how much of an imported cost the euro area absorbs rather than tightens against.

boj-2026-10.standing: Japan's central bank sets the short-term policy rate and manages the yield curve for the world's largest creditor nation. Because Japanese institutions hold vast foreign bond portfolios, its decisions move currencies and debt markets far beyond Tokyo.
boj-2026-10.recent: Tokyo has been weighing whether to steer the yen through pension money, an unusual step that signals how far the currency question has travelled beyond the rate itself. The meeting lands with global bond yields at multi-decade highs and the dollar already weakened by a yen surge, which changes what a move here settles for holders of Japanese debt abroad.

boe-2026-11.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, nine members who meet eight times a year to set Bank Rate. Its votes are published individually, and they set the cost of borrowing for UK households, most of whom refinance mortgages on short fixed terms.
boe-2026-11.recent: The committee meets into a global bond repricing that has pushed yields to multi-decade highs on inflation fears, with oil near $105 a barrel adding a supply-side impulse the MPC cannot reach with rates. What it settles is whether a country whose mortgage market resets on short fixed terms absorbs that through borrowers or through sterling.

fomc-2026-12.standing: The Federal Open Market Committee, the twelve-member body that sets the target range for the US federal funds rate at eight scheduled meetings a year. It is the anchor for dollar borrowing costs worldwide, transmitting through Treasury yields into mortgages, corporate debt and every currency priced against the dollar.
fomc-2026-12.recent: Goldman Sachs abandoned its no-hike call after Houthi forces captured Yemen's port of Mocha and pushed Brent near $110, sending August consumer prices up 0.4% and a payroll surge through the same month. The committee now has to separate a war in the price index from domestic demand, and Waller has already staked out a position against the hawks.

g20-2026-miami.standing: The annual meeting of heads of state and government from the world's largest economies, plus the European Union. It has no treaty powers, so its weight rests on what the leaders in the room agree to say and do together on debt, trade, energy and war.

ecb-2026-12.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council, which sets the main refinancing and deposit rates for the 20 countries sharing the euro. Its decisions set borrowing costs for some 350 million people and transmit through every bank in the bloc.

boe-2026-12.standing: The Bank of England's nine-member Monetary Policy Committee, which votes eight times a year on Bank Rate. That rate sets what British households, savers and firms pay to borrow, and sterling and gilt yields move with the vote.
boe-2026-12.recent: The committee meets on 17 December to decide where borrowing costs sit going into the new year. Each member votes separately and the split is published alongside the decision, so the meeting settles not only the rate itself but how far the committee has moved from where it stood at the previous vote.

boj-2026-12.standing: Japan's central bank, whose policy board sets the short-term rate and the pace of its bond purchases at eight scheduled meetings a year. Because Japanese institutions are the world's largest foreign creditors, its choices carry into bond markets far beyond Tokyo.
boj-2026-12.recent: The board meets after a year in which Tokyo has looked outside monetary policy for the yen, weighing whether pension money can be steered to defend the currency. That question narrows as global bond yields reach multi-decade highs and oil near $105 a barrel feeds an inflation impulse Japan imports rather than generates. What this meeting settles is whether the yen is the Bank's problem or the pension fund's.

fred-us-retail-sales-2026-09-16.standing: The Census Bureau's monthly tally of receipts at US retailers and food services, the first broad read on household spending in a given month. Consumption drives roughly two-thirds of the American economy, so the print moves rate expectations.
